classification.difficultyReason: Calculate two rectangular areas and use the cost per square metre to determine a new cost.

content.prompt: It costs $\$225$ to put grass on a rectangular piece of ground measuring $3\,\mathrm{m}$ by $5\,\mathrm{m}$. How much will it cost to put the same kind of grass on a piece of ground that is $7\,\mathrm{m}$ by $4\,\mathrm{m}$?

answer.short:
$\$420$

Find the cost per square metre, then multiply by the new area.
answer.worked:
Original area:
$$\begin{align*}A_1&=3\times5\\A_1&=15\,\mathrm{m}^2\end{align*}$$
Cost per square metre:
$$\begin{align*}r&=225\div15\\r&=\$15\text{ per }\mathrm{m}^2\end{align*}$$
New area:
$$\begin{align*}A_2&=7\times4\\A_2&=28\,\mathrm{m}^2\end{align*}$$
Total cost:
$$\begin{align*}C&=28\times15\\C&=\$420\end{align*}$$
